title: Lambda Provisioned Concurrency Utilization

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.5.13 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.5.13 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" metric_name="ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.13_lambda_provisioned_concu_13"
| sort -_time
description: Provisioned concurrency is a fixed cost; low utilization wastes spend while high utilization risks cold starts on overflow—balance requires continuous measurement.
value: Detecting lambda provisioned concurrency utilization early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Collect `ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization` for each alias or version with provisioned settings. Compare against provisioned units from tags or CloudFormation export. Alert when utilization is chronically low (cost optimization) or high (risk of throttling on burst beyond provisioned pool).
visualization: Line chart (utilization by function/alias), Area chart (consumed vs provisioned concurrency), Table (FunctionName, util %, recommended units).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Cold starts, retries, and a bad client sending junk traffic can all raise error counts without a code bug. We look at the share of invocations and we compare the same time last week before we assume the function is broken.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect `ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization` for each alias or version with provisioned settings. Compare against provisioned units from tags or CloudFormation export. Alert when utilization is chronically low (cost optimization) or high (risk of throttling on burst beyond provisioned pool).
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/Lambda" metric_name="ProvisionedConcurrencyUtilization"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.13_lambda_provisioned_concu_13"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect lambda provisioned concurrency utilization. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_13_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (utilization by function/alias), Area chart (consumed vs provisioned concurrency), Table (FunctionName, util %, recommended units)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of lambda provisioned concurrency utilization so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
